question: Should this maintainer-requested internal-facade cleanup be approved after a current-main rebase, a passing `check-guards` rerun, and concise runtime proof of the preserved boundaries?
rationale: The protected maintainer label requires explicit human handling, and the supplied evidence does not expose the failed guard’s cause or an inspectable after-fix runtime artifact.

options.title: Refresh and land
options.body: Rebase the branch, clear or explain the guard failure, and approve once the focused import/runtime proof confirms no boundary regression.

options.title: Narrow the refactor
options.body: Retain any facade whose removal exposes an intended public or lazy-loading boundary, then rerun the affected checks.

options.title: Pause the cleanup
options.body: Defer the refactor if current-main drift or guard results show that these facades still protect a needed contract.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch, clear or explain the guard failure, and approve once the focused import/runtime proof confirms no boundary regression.
